description:
STEP 2a (the de-risking half-step, behavior-preserving, stays GREEN).

WHY split: alpha_normalize_vars mints TypeVarId(0,1,2..) from one counter; address_id mints TypeVarId(0,1,2..) from a SEPARATE counter into the SAME TypeVarId space. They collide WITHIN one constructed type. So arrow(old_alpha_inputs, r0_address) is unsafe in one shot -- the result address can equal an input's alpha id and conflate. That coupling is why the one-shot 27.6 probe cascaded to ~30 failures. Splitting container-swap from canonicalization-change dissolves it.

Work (mechanical, identity-preserving):
- ActivationKey { root, function, input: Vec<Ty> } -> { root, function, arrow: Ty }.
- Build it as types.arrow(&current_canonical_inputs, SENTINEL) -- SAME inputs as today (per-input alpha + per-slot convergence_class), so key identity classes are bit-identical (arrow interning is injective in args; constant result suffix changes nothing). Tests stay green.
- SENTINEL result = none(): collision-free (no vars), UNUSED (no consumer reads the result side yet), explicitly scaffolding. 27.6b replaces it with real r0 via address_arrow.
- Add immutable Types::arrow_params(&self, &Ty) -> Vec<Ty> (via descr().pure_arrow().args) and ActivationKey::inputs(&self, &Types) -> Vec<Ty>.
- Rewrite every .input consumer (~12 prod sites incl world.rs activation_inputs/normalize_contributions read paths, root.rs:117, native.rs:357/441/3467, transport.rs:747/776, artifact.rs:314/395, fixture_facts.rs:181, semantic.rs:347/357 + tests) to .inputs(types)/arrow_params.

Outcome: arrow: Ty threaded through the whole system; direct Vec<Ty> field dependence severed; lib+matrix green, zero warnings. Sets up 27.6b to be a purely SEMANTIC diff (swap construction to whole-scope address_arrow).
title: ActivationKey carries arrow: Ty (half-step: thread the arrow, project the input side)
